action.description: Which operation to perform — pass its matching params object below (e.g. action: "health-report" pairs with healthReport: {...}).

conversationId.description: Conversation to diagnose. Self-scoped: the conversation must belong to your own org unless you are Cedar staff.
List executions for this conversation. Self-scoped: the conversation must belong to your own org unless you are Cedar staff.

targetUserId.description: List executions for this user instead of a conversation. Defaults to yourself. Any-account if you are Cedar staff, or a teammate's if you are an org admin/owner in their same organization — a plain member passing a different user's id is rejected.

runId.description: Drill into one run's tool calls instead of listing executions (takes priority over conversationId/targetUserId). Self-scoped by default: the run must belong to you, unless you are Cedar staff or an org admin/owner viewing a teammate's run in your own organization.

limit.description: Max executions to return, max 50 (ignored in runId mode).

runId.description: Run ID to fetch the full debug dump for (execution row, tool calls, sub-agent executions). Self-scoped by default: must be your own run, unless you are Cedar staff or an org admin/owner viewing a teammate's run in your own organization.

toolCallId.description: The `id` of one specific tool call (from execution-detail's toolCalls[] or subAgents[]) to fetch full input/output for. Use this to inspect a sub-agent's own tool calls — execution-detail's subAgents[] lists each sub-agent run but not its tool calls; drill into that sub-agent's own runId via execution-detail first to get its tool-call ids, then call this action per id.

targetUserId.description: Per-user health snapshot for this user (meetings, tasks, agent-execution buckets, derived red/yellow issues). Defaults to yourself. Any-account if you are Cedar staff, or a teammate's if you are an org admin/owner in their same organization. IMPORTANT: this per-user view computes a "post-meeting pipeline degraded" red-flag signal that the org-wide view (pass orgId instead) deliberately skips because it is too expensive to run for every user in an org — always trust THIS view over the org-wide one when you need an authoritative read on one specific account.

orgId.description: Org-wide health snapshot (green/yellow/red status per user in the org) instead of one user's detail. Cedar-staff only. IMPORTANT: this view does NOT compute the post-meeting-pipeline red-flag signal the per-user view (targetUserId) does — a user can show green/yellow here but red when the same action is called again scoped to just that user. Do not report an account as healthy based on this view alone; drill into targetUserId for any account that had recent meetings.

orgAopId.description: Per-user mode only: filter tasks/executions to AOPs under this org_aop_id.

targetUserId.description: The user account this monitor watches.

orgId.description: Org this monitor belongs to, if applicable.

monitorType.description: A slug describing the monitor kind, e.g. "regression", "reinvestigate", "config_verification". Not a DB enum — free text.

triggerConfig.description: Must include `verify_condition` (a plain-English condition the evaluator checks against each new execution) — omitting it makes every future evaluation return "uncertain" instead of ever passing or failing; createMonitor() rejects a call missing it. Conventional keys used by the cedar-configuration skill's config-verification monitors: symptom_class, change_description, verify_condition, original_report, target_executions, event_type_filter.

alertChannel.description: Slack channel or DM to alert when the monitor fires or resolves.

investigationId.description: Ties this monitor to an existing Sherlock investigation row. Omit for monitors not tied to one (e.g. cedar-configuration config-verification monitors).

triggerType.description: "cron" fires exactly ONE named subagent in isolation (requires subagentName). "before_meeting" fires EVERY before-meeting subagent wired to conversationId — not isolated to one subagent, since Cedar has no isolated-single-agent before_meeting path today; this mirrors what a real meeting trigger actually does. "webhook" fires one registered webhook (requires webhookId) through the same dispatch path a real inbound POST or Slack-channel message would take — conversationless, so save-draft/save-slack-draft/task creation are unavailable to whatever it runs.

subagentName.description: cron only. The subagent slug to run, in isolation. Required unless agentId is given instead — provide exactly one of the two.

agentId.description: cron only. Alternative to subagentName: the Agent Workspace agent_id (as shown in the UI, not the document filename). Resolved to its underlying {aopId, subagentName} before running — with targetUserId, this is how an admin runs a teammate's SAVED agent without already knowing its filename. Requires targetUserId when naming an agent that is not your own.

level.description: cron only. "user" reads the subagent from your own AOP; "org" reads it from the org AOP linked to your own AOP (you can only test an org-level agent your own AOP is actually linked to, never an arbitrary other org's).

aopId.description: cron only. Your own AOP id. Omit to auto-resolve when you have exactly one AOP; required if you have more than one.

conversationId.description: Required when triggerType is "before_meeting". Self-scoped: must be a conversation you own.

webhookId.description: Required when triggerType is "webhook". Must be a webhook registered to yourself (or, with targetUserId, to the teammate you are testing).

webhookPayload.description: webhook only. Explicit payload; omitted defaults to `{}`.

deliverForReal.description: Default false: outbound sends (Slack/email/notifications) are suppressed and this returns a preview of what WOULD have been sent. It is NOT a dry run: DB writes (tasks, fields, documents) AND writes to connected systems the agent makes itself (e.g. a HubSpot PATCH through run-code-executor, a Drive edit) still happen. To test without touching a CRM, use the agent's own read-only mode. Set true to actually deliver for real — for an org-level cron agent (level: "org") this requires you to be an org admin/owner, since it posts to a channel your whole team may share; a user-level agent only ever touches your own destinations, so no extra check applies there.

targetUserId.description: Test-run this specific teammate's own subagent instead of yours — their AOP, their conversation ownership, their execution history. Defaults to yourself. Any-teammate only if you are an org admin/owner in the same organization as them; a plain member naming someone else is rejected.

user_request_summary.description: One sentence, in your own words: what the user actually asked you to do in this turn. Used only for Cedar's observability — it does not change what this tool does.

is_new_request.description: true on the FIRST Cedar tool call of a NEW user request; false when this call continues the same request you are already working on. Groups related calls into one activity thread.
